top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation fell 87.50 to 75.00, a contribution of minus 1.875 and the bulk of the day's 1.51 decline: triggered production signals dropped from 7 to 6 out of 8, the only change being gold flipping from up 0.2162 to down 0.0566. The other 6 legs still hold - S&P down, dollar strength, real-rate pressure, bitcoin down, small-cap underperformance and copper down.

AI hardware was the day's only directional event: the equal-weight four-name semis basket fell 4.5118, the worst of 22 rows, with AMD down 8.7545, AVGO down 4.7618 and MU down 2.5212, while NVDA fell only 2.0097. The two substitute beneficiaries that rose against the trend yesterday were today's biggest losers, which points to money leaving the question of who gains from Nvidia's vacancy rather than selling Nvidia alone.

High-yield spreads narrowed 3.3 to 3.2, taking the liquidity and credit dimension from 71.14 to 66.76 for a contribution of minus 0.876, the largest offset of the day; yet the 3.2 level still maps to a 72.36 percentile risk score, so credit is not confirming the equity selloff.

The 10-year rose to 5.1, the real rate to 2.86 and the 2-year to 4.86, making macro the highest-scoring dimension at 77.61; all three are the 2026-11-12 FRED vintage and today's Treasury closes are not yet booked, so rate risk is understated rather than overstated.

Breadth improved from 54 to 56 names out of 155, yet new lows among 157 rose from 10 to 13 while new highs held at 2: the median improved while the tail deteriorated, which is index-level dispersion rather than a broad decline.

supporting_signals.claim: Crypto weakened in step: bitcoin fell 4.3998 to 68341, ether fell 4.4191 to 1927.16 and SOL fell 3.4511 to 78.67, with bitcoin dominance at 0.589204. This is a risk-appetite contraction running with the US AI complex, not an independent crypto event.

Of 22 rows, 18 fell and 4 rose, mean down 1.5865 and median down 1.4525, the four best directions being fintech up 2.4693, gaming up 1.4180, digital advertising up 0.8266 and data centres up 0.2216: money did not leave, it rotated inside the complex.

All 11 A-share names fell, mean down 4.2904 and median down 3.8909, the worst being 688008.SH at 7.3178; the last daily bar behind this reading is dated 2026-11-13 with a non-null close, so it is the full Asian-session pricing of this governance shock.

contradicting_signals.claim: The score fell 1.51 and the tape fell too; the directions agree but the causes do not: almost the entire decline came from cross-asset and gold, while the equity dimension contributed plus 0.314. Read alone, the total reads as risk falling, when in fact an equity selloff was masked by one precious-metal quote flipping.

On the same day the semis basket fell 4.5118, breadth improved from 54 to 56 names and 4 directions rose: this is a single-point repricing of AI hardware, not broad risk aversion. Calling today a market-wide selloff would hide the structure.

Today's drop sits inside a strong week: AMD is still up 18.9337 over one week, AVGO up 18.1552 and MU up 12.7986, with only NVDA down 12.7465. A single-day drawdown is not yet a trend reversal; the test is whether next week recovers it.

The late_cycle label is a threshold fallthrough, not a momentum signal: risk_off stopped firing only because breadth at 0.3613 sits 1.13 percentage points above the 0.35 trigger, after which the cross-asset 0.75 with VIX 18.7 branch took over. Reading the label as a cycle call over-interprets it.

bull_case.title: Governance shock absorbed by rotation
points: 4 of the 22 rows still rose, fintech up 2.4693 and gaming up 1.4180, showing money rotating inside the complex rather than leaving.
Breadth improved from 54 to 56 names; there is no structural damage at the index level.
High-yield spreads narrowed to 3.2; credit is not confirming the equity selloff.

base_case.title: Single-point repricing of AI hardware
points: The 22 rows averaged down 1.5865 with a median of 1.4525, heavily concentrated in semis and AI infrastructure.
The 11th consecutive high_risk session, with macro the top dimension at 77.61; rates are background pressure rather than today's trigger.

bear_case.title: Rates and AI valuation hit together
points: The 10-year at 5.1 and the real rate at 2.86, and neither reading includes today's Treasury close, so the real pressure may be larger.
New lows among 157 rose to 13 while new highs held at 2; the tail is deteriorating and the breadth improvement is not solid.
If the beneficiary trade is being unwound wholesale, AMD's and AVGO's 18.9337 and 18.1552 weekly gains become the next source of supply.
